items.headline: Nobel Prize in Chemistry awarded for discovering self-amplifying chemical reactions
items.summary: Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai won the twenty twenty six Nobel Prize in Chemistry for discovering how to make chemical reactions build an excess of one mirror-image molecule over the other, including a reaction that amplifies itself almost perfectly. The work underpins how chemists make pure, single-handed molecules used in modern medicines.
items.why_it_matters: These methods let drugmakers reliably produce the correct molecular form of a medicine instead of a mix that can be less effective or even harmful.
items.source_name: Nobel Prize (Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences)
